results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: Where Did Six Minutes Go? ¶3
results.finding: Marked two_ideas, but the two questions are parallel members of one idea (Ingrid's two unanswered questions), exactly the spec's p07 and the pair the conclusion answers.

results.quote: The objectives in the table are the targets Veldmark set in 2027; the search and event figures follow [[search-architecture]] and [[event-driven-listings]].
results.finding: The reverse outliner needed two summaries: where the table's objectives come from, and how ended listings are rendered (decided by web-and-SEO from the reason, which the pipeline carries). No sentence joins them; a lead such as 'Two things in the table are set elsewhere' (objectives by the search and event chapters, rendering by web-and-SEO) would make one idea, with the pipeline's job as carrying the reason.

Every paragraph ties to a supporting claim: intro and scene to S2-S4 (the unmeasured held share, the unmeasured removal path, stacked timers); concepts to S1-S2 (leboncoin and Which? to the moderation mode and the gate); architecture to S1 and S4 (ordering rules, zombies); unpublish to S4 (expiry via p25-p26); observability to S5; In Practice to S2-S4; verticals to S2; trade-offs, failure modes, CA view and questions to S1-S5; conclusion synthesizes S2, S4 and S5.

Each example, case, table, figure and quotation is framed by a sentence saying what it shows: baseline table (p35 lead, then p36-p37 findings), Figure 1 (p37 timers), stage table (p09), Essen Golf ('An SLA that does not separate the clocks blames the wrong team'), leboncoin and Which? (point-first rule sentences, reinforced in p49), Figure 2 (p15 lead), Vinted 2021 ('for the same reason'), Figure 3 (p24), 41,000 audit ('You cannot propagate a removal to a copy you do not know exists'), consumer table (p29), digests (p30), mobile.de renewalDate (the renewal rule it illustrates), Google expiry (p26 last sentence), Figure 5 (p31), Vinted 2023/2024 ('Two lessons transfer'), engine docs ('commit frequency is a capacity decision'), SLA card, budget table (p39 lead; its placement is a flow finding), plan ('shape gives most of the gain'), bike test, vertical table (p42-p43), Barcelona ring, trade-off table (p44).

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary. Spot checks: p03 contrast ('Neighboring chapters own the parts'), p07 contrast ('not how to make each stage faster'), p35 cause_effect ('To see where the six minutes went'), architecture problem_solution ('Because mixing the two questions slows pipelines'), p21 contrast ('In the fan-out design'), unpublish contrast ('mirror image ... but'), p14 additional_support ('A second rule governs edits'), p25 sequence ('ends the listings no seller ends'), p31 similarity ('exactly as it would for a sale'), failure modes contrast ('Without the design's rules'), conclusion conclusion_summary ('Ingrid's two questions ... have one answer'), p53 contrast. Note: p38 now opens 'To answer her two questions' (accepted in the decision log), while the spec's p38 transition_in still names 'the three findings' as carried over; the problem_solution relationship is expressed either way, but the spec's carries_over is stale.

Both flow readers describe the same organising principle as the spec (problem_solution: the scene's case and two questions, concepts, publish then unpublish, proof, application to the case, generalization, then grouped closing judgements), and neither marks any section's position unclear. The material lost-thread points are recorded as separate results.

The conclusion answers the scene's questions and gives a course of action, then hands off; it does not open with 'in conclusion', restate the thesis alone, add a new subtopic beyond the declared hand-off, or hold body evidence.

States what no section states alone: both of Ingrid's questions have one answer, 'write down what the pipeline counts', with the SLA card and the registry resting on the record's definition of published; so-what: 'one owner can promise the path there and back again and prove it per consumer'.
Returns to Ingrid's two questions by name and to the opening's 'and back again' ('promise the path there and back again').

The cold reader's predicted order matches the roadmap item for item (scene and 214 digests; stages, clocks, moderation modes; decision and propagation paths with ordering rules; registry, re-checks, expiry, takedowns; proof; others' gains then the 90-second budget; verticals; trade-offs; failure modes; CA view; questions) and names the evidence kinds (public engineering records, engine documentation, a French judgment, a consumer test, fictional Veldmark).

The answer names coverage (gate-cleared only, the held 6% with their own objective and the held share beside it) and the clock, and for the digest: snapshot assembled in advance and never re-checked; registry with removal objective and owner; removal events with version gating and tombstones; send-time re-check; acknowledgements to the propagation monitor. All parts of the expected answer.

The answer says not every listing should wait; chooses per listing by risk (high-risk tiers such as a new account's rentals in fake-rental cities wait, the rest go live and the check runs after, where it can demote, hold or remove); places the check in the 30-second parallel async-checks row; asks which stage's budget pays, decided on the SLA card at the architecture forum; and keeps the held objective and held share. Matches the expected answer.
